subtopic_detail: Quintero stage III at 20 weeks in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy
stem:
You are the obstetric registrar in a regional unit assessing a 27-year-old G1 at 20+2 weeks with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy. Fortnightly surveillance scanning today shows twin one deepest vertical pocket of 1.4 cm with an empty bladder, and twin two deepest vertical pocket of 9.2 cm with a full bladder. Twin one umbilical artery Doppler shows absent end-diastolic flow. Twin two shows a reversed a-wave in the ductus venosus. Both twins are alive with normal biometry and no structural anomaly. Cervical length is 34 mm.

The woman is well. The nearest tertiary fetal medicine unit performing fetoscopic laser is 4 hours by air.

data_table.Vital signs: pulse 78, blood pressure 108/68, respiratory rate 14, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.5 degrees Celsius
data_table.Bloods: Hb 122 g/L (110-140), platelets 245 x10^9/L (150-400), group A positive on file
data_table.Imaging: MCDA twins, twin one DVP 1.4 cm bladder empty UA AEDF, twin two DVP 9.2 cm bladder full DV reversed a-wave, cervix 34 mm closed

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Weekly amnioreduction of the polyhydramniotic sac at the regional unit until viability at 24 weeks
options.rationale: Amnioreduction alone is inferior to fetoscopic laser for stage II and above TTTS between 16 and 26 weeks and should not delay referral to a laser centre. (Source: ISUOG TTTS Guideline)

options.text: Urgent transfer today to the tertiary fetal medicine unit for consideration of fetoscopic laser photocoagulation
options.rationale: Quintero stage III TTTS at 16 to 26 weeks has best survival with fetoscopic laser ablation of placental anastomoses, and delay worsens outcomes; urgent transfer to a laser-capable centre is standard care. (Source: ISUOG TTTS Guideline)

options.text: Selective feticide of the donor twin by cord occlusion at the regional unit under ultrasound guidance
options.rationale: Selective reduction is a last-line option when laser fails or is technically impossible, and should not be offered as first step in a viable stage III pregnancy with laser available. (Source: ISUOG TTTS Guideline)

options.text: Give corticosteroids and admit for continuous CTG monitoring until spontaneous delivery in the coming days
options.rationale: Steroids and monitoring are inappropriate at 20 weeks (previable) and do not address the underlying vascular anastomoses driving TTTS; laser therapy targets the pathology. (Source: ISUOG TTTS Guideline)

options.text: Reassure and repeat the scan in 2 weeks because Quintero stage III often improves spontaneously without treatment
options.rationale: Untreated stage III TTTS carries a very high mortality for both twins and does not resolve spontaneously; a two week delay would risk both fetuses. (Source: ISUOG TTTS Guideline)

explanation.summary: TTTS in monochorionic twins is diagnosed by oligohydramnios in the donor sac (DVP under 2 cm) and polyhydramnios in the recipient (DVP over 8 cm before 20 weeks). Quintero stage III adds abnormal Doppler in either twin. Between 16 and 26 weeks, fetoscopic laser photocoagulation is superior to amnioreduction. Urgent transfer to a laser-capable centre saves both twins. Untreated stage III TTTS has very high dual mortality.
key_points: TTTS diagnosis: DVP under 2 cm donor plus over 8 cm recipient before 20 weeks
Quintero stage III adds abnormal UA, DV or umbilical vein Doppler
Fetoscopic laser is first line for stage II and above between 16 and 26 weeks
Untreated stage III TTTS has around 80 to 90 percent dual mortality
explanation.pearls: ISUOG uses DVP over 8 cm before 20 weeks and over 10 cm after 20 weeks for the polyhydramnios threshold; laser survival is around 65 percent for both twins and 88 percent for at least one twin, compared with under 30 percent survival with expectant management for stage III.
